newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MADAR GETS CHANCE IN ATTACK AGAINST TURKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MADAR GETS CHANCE IN ATTACK AGAINST TURKS.

text.p: France, who were let down at the European championship by their lack of a killer punch up front, continue their quest for a World Cup goalscorer in a friendly against Turkey at the Parc des Princes on Wednesday.

Coach Aime Jacquet, deprived of three injured strikers he would normally have picked, will test the recalled Mickael Madar of Spain's Deportivo La Coruna and may also give 26-year-old Franck Gava of Lyon a run as substitute.
Metz striker Robert Pires, who came off the bench for his debut in the 2-0 friendly win over Mexico in August, could also be given another game as substitute.
Jacquet, in an experimental first season of two before France host the 1998 World Cup finals, will also try out some options in his more settled midfield and defence.

"I have two objectives for this match against Turkey," he said. "To innovate by allowing young players to become integrated into this group and to enrich a squad which has played together for some time now, is very competitive...and in which I have great confidence."

With Paris St Germain's Alain Roche pulling out of the squad on Tuesday because of injury, uncapped Alain Goma of French champions Auxerre will play in central defence, while Sampdoria midfielder Christian Karembeu plays at right back.
AC Milan's Marcel Desailly is suffering from pains in his calf and will not play.
Neither Jacquet nor Reynald Pedros are concerned that the Parisian crowd might again give the Marseille midfielder, jeered against Mexico and substituted at halftime, a poor reception.

The Turks, in two matches under new coach Mustafa Denizli who replaced Fatih Terim after Euro 96, have beaten Moldova 2-0 in a friendly, then lost 2-1 away to Belgium in their opening World Cup group seven qualifier on August 31.

They are without playmaker Sergen Yalcin, suspended after being sent off against Belgium, and Tugay Kerimolgu for disciplinary reasons. Trabzonspor's 30-year-old midfielder Unal Karaman is back after three years.

Turkey impressed with their industry and some measure of skill at Euro 96 -- their first European championship finals -- particularly left-sided midfielder Abdullah Ercan of Trabzonspor, who has 30 caps.
But, playing with just Galatasaray striker Hakan Sukur up front, the Turks failed to score in three defeats and will be looking to try attacking options against France.

France - 16-Fabien Barthez; 17-Christian Karembeu, 5-Laurent Blanc, 4-Alain Goma, 15-Lilian Thuram; 14-Sabri Lamouchi, 7-Didier Deschamps, 10-Zinedine Zidane, 8-Reynald Pedros; 6-Youri Djorkaeff, 9-Mickael Madar.

Turkey (from) - Rustu Recber, Engin Ipekoglu; Erkan Avseren, Recep Cetin, Bulent Korkmaz, Vedat Inceefe, Alpay Ozalan, Ogun Temizkanoglu; Oguz Cetin, Serdar Topraktepe, Mehmet Ozdilek, Celil Sagir, Abdullah Ercan, Tolunay Kafkas, Unal Karaman; Arif Erdem, Hakan Sukur, Saffet Sancakli.
